correctness.rationale: For q any prime power and a>=b>=2, orthogonality over maps W->kerX reduces the Fourier multiplier to exact-kernel injective-map sums. Subspace Möbius inversion and the Gaussian binomial theorem yield S_K(A)=(-1)^r q^{binom(b-d,2)} product_{j=a-b+d+1}^{a-r}(q^j-1). The K=0 term has exact q-divisibility exponent binom(b,2) and quotient (-1)^b mod q; all d>=1 terms gain d(a-b)+binom(d+1,2)>=1 factors of q. Therefore no coefficient is zero. Rank-b A and B attain the least modulus. Complete exact checks for (q,a,b)=(2,2,2),(2,3,2),(2,3,3),(3,2,2),(4,2,2) agree; finite checks are not the general proof.
